newsitem.title: UK: Brazil CS sugar output likely to exceed 95/96 -Man.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CS sugar output likely to exceed 95/96 -Man.

text.p: Sugar output in Brazil's centre-south region in 1996/97 should still be higher than last year's 9.8 million tonnes tel quel but concern over the alcohol quota could trim the excess, trade house E D & F Man said on Friday.

In its August monthly report, Man said sugar production in the centre-south stood at just over 43 percent of the authorised production of 10.47 million tonnes tel quel whilst alcohol output had reached almost 45 percent of the authorised figure.
"By contrast, lst year there was more of a bias towards sugar production at the expense of alcohol," the report said.
"This suggests that although centre-south production is still likely to exceed last year's final figure...it may not be by so much as some have speculated."
The Man report added that Brazil would have to import alcohol despite signs that quotas were being more readily filled by producers this year.
The Brazilian government recently announced a reduction of the import duty on alcohol to zero for a quota of 700 million litres valid for one year from August 28, Man said.
